I moderate /v/tesla and /v/hyperloop. The DDoS delays and breaking mobile clients are bad enough, but the new limits on subverse submission are just too much for me.

First it was a 10 submission in 24 hours per subverse limit, which I came up against several times. Now the system is limiting me to three posts to my own subverse per hour?!? I typically have time for one session per day to sit down and post all the Tesla and Hyperloop news I can scrape from the last 24 hours. I don't have the ability to be here several times throughout the day.

While I'm hoping that others will eventually contribute to my subverses, so far I haven't reached that critical mass. I built /v/tesla from 20 or so subscribers to over 400 at current count by posting high quality OC day in and day out. Look at my stats. I've been working hard to make voat a better place.

I think these submission limits are generally a great idea, but not for mods in their own subverses. Mods should be exempt. I've spent a lot of hours feeding this data and trying to make voat a better place, only to get shackled as a result. It's quite insulting (though I understand there are general reasons for limits). These limits should simply not apply to mods in their own subverses.

I'll be taking a break from voat in protest. Voat is now broken for me. If the limits are lifted for mods in their own subverses, I'll be back. In the meantime, I'll be looking around for other forums to support and if I find one that show promise like voat does, my break may become permanent.
I post lots of OC in several subverses. For me, voat was just broken. Submission limits in subverses that I mod should go away or I'm done here

Wow! Really? I'm posting how the site is broken for me (and many others) and that's your response? Are you just trolling here to get people to leave voat? That's how it seems to me. Just wow.

Mods need to be able to post in their own subs. Your response is just unnecessarily snide. Remember that voat is created by the community and the community has the right to suggest rule changes.
I saw this complaint in a few other places as well. I can't imagine who at Voat thought this was a good idea to implement without excluding mods.
The limit should at least be raised for mods in their own sub

That's what I'd advocate for as well. Don't give mods total posting power, unless they're posting in their own sub. I know this is a non issue for most subs, but there are a fair number of subs that mods post in very frequently, not to mention some subs that are entirely posts from the sole moderator. It doesn't make sense to impose this rule on somebody in their own sub, especially in this stage where so many subs are barely starting out.

The issue is that if mods had unlimited or even expanded posting privileges, it would basically result in spamming /v/all. Having said that, imagine that power in the hands of someone unscrupulous. All they would have to do is create a subverse with the very intention of spamming /v/all with garbage posts.

It's a simple matter to put a requirement that subverses have a certain number of subscribers to make it to the /v/all listing. That would stop any subverse creation simply for spamming /v/all. Low subscriber count = not listed at /v/all. Pretty easy.

Then it would no longer be /v/all. It would be /v/some. Beyond that, /v/all is a new subverse's best friend. It gains you vital exposure which hopefully leads to new subscribers. Regardless of the size of the subverse /v/all is limited to, there would still be the potential for abuse if mods were not limited in posting. It wouldn't even necessarily have to be intentional abuse. Imagine a mod decides to make a very large number of posts. /v/all is suddenly flooded with a single subverse's posts.

abuse is always possible without some base level of quality. I could create a dozen new subverses, and post three items each to get 36 new posts into /v/all without filtering, so it really is required. We already have filtering in /v/all. From my mod settings page: "WARNING: if you set minimum CCP to a value higher than 0, your subverse will be hidden from /v/all." The precedent is there.

It's cool though. It's not like this community is going to grow in a healthy way with only two guys running it. It's not like any easy registration/no filter community like this that gets popular isn't immediately swarmed by shills and propaganda, massively lowering the signal to noise ratio. I think voat is doomed anyway, honestly. I'm looking elsewhere. I think a site like this takes group of at least 20 dedicated people, enforcing/coding technical standards set by a non-profit board of perhaps 50 set up to insure the long term health of the space. Without that, I think you get a low quality cesspool or just teeter around before you crash as soon as you get noticed as being something of value. voat is in the latter, heading fast for the former without some major changes implemented very quickly.

edit: I get that /v/all is beneficial to new subs, but cross-posting works well too. That's how I built /v/tesla to 400 users in a month. I cross-posted juicy bits to the /v/technology subverse and elsewhere with a note in the title that it was a "x-post from /v/tesla". That strategy works well and honestly is the best way to build a viewership. Post to a more generalized area that you have a more specialized interest group. Everything stays on-topic and everyone is happy.

You need a dedicated team of perhaps 20 solid coders and another team running admin. Since you don't have millions to purchase all of that (at least not without VC and their controls coming into the game), you should really consider making the whole thing a non-profit, opening up your source as a github-type project and setting up a board of perhaps 30 to handle policy and admin for the site. I get this means you don't get a 250 million dollar payday by selling out, but it does offer the best way to deliver solid growth while avoiding the reddit trap. I just don't see a way past your current dilemma without this kind of game plan. The only other path forward is to get a big dump of VC into the mix and that is guaranteed to destroy your future, sooner or later.

Just my honest opinion. I do wish you guys well and I really hope you are able to keep this space away from the evils of commercialization/shills/propaganda. You do need to make some kind of move if you want this space to make it to the next level, and fast. I hope you choose the path of doing what is best for the long term health and survival of the community and avoid the commercialization trap. Best wishes and good luck! :)
